title: docs(getting-started): the tutorial's Resolve action resolves the ticket; one routing line opens the index
body:
Fixes #22152
Fixes #22165
Clause-②: no

Docs only: five pages under `content/docs/getting-started/`. Nothing publishes, so there is no changeset (`skip-changeset`).

## What changed

### The tutorial's Resolve button now resolves the ticket (anchor card)

`build-with-claude-code.mdx` step 3 wrote `resolve_ticket` as a `type: 'script'` action with `target: 'resolveTicket'`, and nothing registered that handler. The action is now the declarative single-record field write the spec already has:

```ts
operation: 'update',
patch: { status: 'resolved' },
```

(`type` is left at its default `'script'`, as `ActionSchema` asks for this shape.) A short paragraph under the code says what the action does and what a `target` handler would need instead. Step 5 now asks the reader to click **Resolve** and names what they should see: the *Ticket resolved.* toast, the status changing to **Resolved**, the button disappearing, and the ticket leaving **Support → Open**.

`quick-start.mdx` (Anatomy) has no action code of its own; its "Reading the other pieces → Actions" bullet now tells a reviewer to check what a click does (declarative `operation`/`patch`, an inline `body`, or a `target` whose handler something registers), and that an unregistered `target` passes `os validate` and is named only by the `os dev` boot warning. Its "How you verify" line now says to click an action.

### One routing line at the top of the Get Started index

`index.mdx` opens with the maintainer's routing line, in the page's language: **Start here:** want an agent to write the app → Build with Claude Code; want to write it by hand and understand every file → Your First Project. The four entry pages' opening callouts now follow it, all in the same shape: each names its place relative to that line and links back to it.

- Build with Claude Code: "The agent path". Points to Your First Project for the by-hand path, and keeps Anatomy as the map.
- Your First Project: "The by-hand path". Points to Build with Claude Code for the agent path.
- Anatomy of an ObjectStack App: "The map, not a starting point". Routes to the two paths, and keeps the Example Apps pointer.
- How AI Development Works: "The why, not a starting point". Routes to the two paths. It had no callout before; its trailing "for the hands-on walkthrough" sentence became this callout.

## Why the declarative route, measured

Both routes from the triage direction were measured against a project freshly scaffolded with the published `create-objectstack@17.7.0` (`--template blank`; the same 17.7.0 as `main`'s package versions):

- **Declarative `operation: 'update'` + `patch`**: a 4-line change to the action. It needs no new file, and the config is not edited, so the page's existing sentence "the config is not edited" stays true. The write runs as the caller, so permissions, hooks and validations apply as they would to an edit.
- **A handler the tutorial also writes**: a new handler file, plus a named `onEnable` export in `objectstack.config.ts`. The scaffolded config carries none, and its own comment names `onEnable` as the place. That contradicts the page's "the config is not edited" paragraph, and the handler's `ctx.engine` runs elevated, which bypasses row-level security. This route was costed from the scaffolded config. It was not booted.

On the four axes:
- **Real use**: the runtime executor and the Console's `ActionRunner` both read `operation` before `type` (liveness ledger `operation`/`patch`: `live`; objectui pin `a58626c88d` `executeUpdateOperation`).
- **Long-term fit**: the shape is metadata only, with no code.
- **AI error-proofing**: `ActionSchema` refuses `target`/`body` beside `operation: 'update'`, so the shape cannot regress into the dead-button form.
- **Scope**: it adds no new surface and no new gate. As triage directed, no lint rule is added.

## Evidence

All runs used a project scaffolded with `npx create-objectstack@17.7.0 support-desk --template blank --skip-skills`. Step 3's four files were extracted **verbatim** from the page by a script, and the four barrel export lines were added. The extraction from this branch's head is byte-identical to the files measured below (`diff -r` clean).

| | before (`main` page) | after (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| `os validate` | `✓ Validation passed` · `Data: 2 Objects  6 Fields` · `UI: 1 Apps  1 Views  1 Actions` | same: `✓ Validation passed (211ms)`, same counts |
| `tsc --noEmit` in the project | not run | exit 0 |
| `os dev --ui` boot diagnostics | 4 warnings, including `WARN [action-governance] declared script actions with NO handler … {"count":1,"actions":["support_desk_ticket:resolve_ticket"]}` | 3 warnings; `grep -c action-governance` = **0** |
| REST click: `POST /api/v1/actions/support_desk_ticket/resolve_ticket {recordId}` | `HTTP 404` `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` "Action 'resolve_ticket' on object 'support_desk_ticket' not found"; status stays `open` | `HTTP 200` `{"success":true,"data":{"operation":"update",…,"status":"resolved"}}`; GET reads `status: resolved` |
| Console click (headless Chromium, published console in `@objectstack/cli@17.7.0`) | not driven (the route answers 404) | create a ticket, then click **Resolve** in the record header: 1 Resolve button before, toast `Ticket resolved.` seen, STATUS reads `Resolved`, 0 Resolve buttons after, the Console POSTed the route (200), and the ticket is absent from **Support → Open** after reload |
| MCP `run_action` (API key, `tools/call`) | not run | `"ok": true`, `"operation": "update"`; GET reads `status: resolved` |

Step 4's transcript still holds with the new action shape. Putting a bare `visible: 'status != "resolved"'` on the declarative action makes `os validate` exit 1 with the same message the page shows: ``stack · action 'resolve_ticket' visible: bare reference `status` … Write `record.status`.`` (`rule: expression-invalid`).

The "before" column is the reverse direction of the same measurement. The only difference between the runs is the page's action block.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived the same 40 commands at this branch's head as at dispatch. All 40 ran after the final commit, at `9bfd965329`, and all exited **0**.

`dispatch-gates --ran` reports: `40 derived, 40 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (a derived zero: every line records an exit code).

On the first pass, two gates refused with exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, so nothing was measured: `check:docs-transcript-drift` needed `@objectstack/lint` built, and `check:skill-examples` needed `@objectstack/client-react` built. Both packages were built through `os-verify-lock.sh` (`VERDICT command-exit 0` both times), and both gates were re-run green.

The five pages also compile with `@mdx-js/mdx` 3.1.1 (a syntax smoke test). `check:doc-anchors` resolves the new `/docs/ui/actions#give-it-server-behavior--two-paths` link (`460 internal #fragment link(s) … all resolve`).

## Scope

- Not here: the other on-ramp items on these pages tracked in #22156 (the index's pnpm floor, the Examples count, the tutorial's "Once it's clean" transcript). That card is serial after this PR, and #22156 is not addressed here.
- No new lint rule or gate, per triage. An authoring-time refusal of a handler-less `target` would be a new gate, and the default for that is no.

## Acceptance notes

- **The `field-no-consumers` warning for the tutorial's `description` field.** #22156 item 6 tracks it. On the published 17.7.0 Console, the **Create Ticket** form does render a Description textarea, while the warning's verdict reads "nothing in this stack reads or displays it … inert". Whoever takes that item may want this measurement before choosing between "place `description` on a view" and "show the warning".
- **Server-side `visible`.** A second REST POST of `resolve_ticket` on an already-resolved ticket answers 200 and rewrites the same value. `visible` hides the button in the UI and is not a server-side guard. The write is idempotent here.
- **Two more observations went to the report** for the seat, not this PR: the Create form leaves the `default: true` select options unselected, and a fresh boot logs a `sys_migration` UNIQUE WARN. Neither touches these pages.
